title: Recipe 12 — Eval Harness (a dataset, a grader, and a number you can defend)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Recipe 12 is where an agent stops being a demo. A labelled split, a grader, a confidence interval — and a gate you can put in CI.”

beats.label: Blank the scratch spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe is never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — scoring samples means really calling the model, once per sample.

groups.title: Beat 1 · Step 1 — two ways to run an eval, two spec shapes

beats.label: Type the agent under test
beats.cue: “crewhaus eval grades a plain target: cli spec — six lines. The dataset and graders are flags, not spec fields.”

beats.label: Now the target: eval shape
beats.cue: “Same agent, different target. This one folds the data and the graders into the spec, and compiles to a standalone scorer.”

beats.label: Point at the data and the grader
beats.cue: “The dataset is a registry reference — name, version, split — not a file path. And exact_match, because inside an eval spec `name` doubles as the type.”

groups.title: Beat 2 · Steps 1.5 and 2 — prove the stack, then author the data

beats.label: Run the in-process eval probe
beats.cue: “Five probes over the dataset registry, the grader registry, the regression runner and the prompt optimizer — no model calls, under two seconds. If this fails, nothing downstream is worth debugging.”

verify.note: measured: all five probes pass in ~0.35s, keyless — includes the test-split lock and an injected regression that correctly fails the gate

beats.label: Type the recipe's dataset
beats.cue: “Three splits, one purpose each: train shapes the agent, dev is for development grading, test is the go/no-go you spend once.”

beats.label: Lint the dataset before spending a token
beats.cue: “Duplicate ids, empty golds, a gold-needing grader over a dataset with no golds, canary contamination — all caught offline. --strict makes it a CI gate.”

verify.note: measured: hello-eval@v1 — 0 errors, 0 warnings, clean. A bare registry ref resolves train+dev only; the test split stays locked

beats.label: Verify the recorded identity — and watch it refuse
beats.cue: “The recipe's illustration ships sampleHashes empty, so verify reports five mismatches and exits 1. That is the check working: a hand-edited dataset file is not the dataset the registry recorded.”

verify.note: deliberate non-zero. Measured: “verify hello-eval@v1: 5 hash mismatch(es)” — stored (none) != actual, once per sample, because the doc fixture's sampleHashes is {}. The sanctioned authoring path is `crewhaus datasets put`, which records the hashes as it writes

beats.label: Type the whole graders grammar
beats.cue: “Five lines and every knob is here: the combine policy, the weighted-mode cut, and one entry with an explicit type. The top level is strict — a typo'd passing_treshold is a parse error, not a silently ignored policy.”

beats.label: Card the measurement instrument
beats.cue: “The grader file is the instrument. Card it, and you get its hash — the identity that run history and baseline pins are keyed on.”

verify.note: offline — parses the file and renders it; also the cheapest proof the graders.yaml is valid

beats.label: Read the card
beats.cue: “combine: all, one deterministic grader, and a gradersHash. Edit the graders file and that hash moves — which is the system telling you your numbers are no longer comparable.”

beats.label: Lint the eval spec
beats.cue: “Parse plus the IR passes the compile path skips — nothing emitted yet.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “Dataset reference, grader list, fan-out — three things the emitted bundle passes to runEval as separate arguments.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target eval — dataset ref, graders, concurrency

beats.label: Compile the scorer — and check it
beats.cue: “--check asserts the shape, installs the deps, and boots it: GREEN with no key, gated on the dataset it declares rather than failing.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok (3 anchors); install ok; boot gated (boot reached its eval dataset gate — the bundle's boot resolves the registry itself)

beats.label: Open the emitted scorer
beats.cue: “It imports runEval, resolves the registry, applies the graders, prints the score. No eval framework in the loop — just this file.”

groups.title: Beat 5 · Step 4 — score the dev split

beats.label: Run the compiled scorer
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The bundle drives the real runEval.” runId, pass rate, and the 95% interval beside it — because at n=2 the point estimate alone is a lie.

verify.note: needs Anthropic credentials — one model call per sample. Reports passRate with a Wilson interval and meanScore with a Student-t interval, and omits them rather than fabricating when n is too small

beats.label: Score the same agent through the CLI
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Same agent, same data, same grader, no bundle in the loop — and --seed 42 so the grader and sampling are reproducible.”
beats.command: crewhaus eval live/agent.cli.yaml --dataset registry:hello-eval --graders live/graders.yaml --concurrency 2 --seed 42 -o live/eval

verify.note: needs Anthropic credentials. Writes per-sample transcript.jsonl / events.jsonl / grades.json plus an index.html report under live/eval, and appends the run to .crewhaus/evals/index.jsonl

groups.title: One more thing · Step 9 — size the dataset before you pay for it

beats.label: Ask what n it would actually take
beats.cue: “Six samples told us the harness works. This tells us what it would cost to believe the number: 385 samples for ±5 points, and 769 if you want to compare two runs.”

verify.note: pure arithmetic, no model and no dataset needed. Measured: n = 385 at 95%/±5pp worst-case p=0.5, ~769 per run for a two-run comparison, and it says out loud that it sizes an estimate's width, not a test's power
